dscr: It is late in the eleventh century and western Europe is beginning to rise from its long darkness. Powerful kingdoms have emerged out of the petty tribal territories of the dark ages, and ambitious kings seek out new lands to expand their domains. Five great powers are set to clash across the continent, and only one will emerge dominant.

The great civilizations of both west and east are set to clash over the fate of this great continent. While the ambitious European kingdoms vie for dominance, the ancient Byzantine Empire struggles against both Arabs and Turks. In the meantime, the Russian Tzar steadies his grip on the vast steppes and the Moors make inroads into southern Europe.

The year is 1050 AD and powerful nations stand ready to lay their claims on the prosperous isles of Britain. The ambitious William of Normandy yearns for the English crown, but King Edward is sure to defend it by any means. In the meantime, the Vikings seek to rebuild the empire of Canute the Great, while the Scots assert their ancient right to these lands.

Long isolated from the rest of Europe, Ireland is one of the last strongholds of Celtic culture. For more than a thousand years the Irish have lived here, with little outside interference. Now the Vikings have landed on its shores, challenging the ancient rights of the kings of Ireland. Who among them will have the strength to unite this isle once and for all?

Spain stands at a crossroads, its future uncertain. The southern provinces are dominated by Islamic Moors, while the north lies in the hands of strong but divided Christian kingdoms. The Moors seek nothing less than dominion over all of Spain, a task they once nearly completed. It will take a strong king to unite the north and drive them out.

Few places on Earth have seen more warfare than the Italian peninsula. Since the fall of Rome, many warlords have tried to claim it, both for its riches and its symbolic value as the heart of the Roman Empire. It now lies in its most precarious state, contested by a volatile mix of powerful kingdoms. Which among them will bring peace to this weary land?

While the kingdoms of western Europe often consider themselves the centre of civilization, the true superpowers of the world lie in the east. It is here that the ultimate fate of the continent will be decided, as the great empires of the Turks, Arabs and Byzantines collide. Only time will tell which of these giants will prove triumphant.
